assumptions: Semi-honest adversaries only: the configuration is popsicle's semi-honest circuit PSI (PsiGarbler/PsiEvaluator implement swanky_adversary::SemiHonest). Nothing here measures or claims malicious security.
The adversarial rows are operational tests of refusal, abort and timeout handling, sampled; they are not a proof of security against an active adversary.
Loopback TCP on one host: latency and bandwidth are not those of a network between independently controlled hosts.
Inputs are synthetic and public; element width is 8 bytes for every fixture.
Protocol randomness comes from SwankyRng::new() in each role (rand::random, OS entropy); no seed is printed, stored or accepted.
The host is shared: load averages before and after are recorded; timings measured under load are not idle-machine timings.

build.cargo_config_toml:
[build]
rustflags = [
    "-C", "target-cpu=native", "--cfg", "vectoreyes_target_cpu_native", "-C", "link-args=-flto"
]
# Pass --html-in-header flags to rustdoc. See the script for details.
rustdoc = "./etc/rustdoc-wrapper.sh"

toolchain.selected_by: rust-toolchain file / rustup default in the build directory

execution_modes.local-threads: one process, two threads, Unix socket pair (the upstream composition)
execution_modes.tcp-process: two OS processes on one host over loopback TCP, each holding only its own input file, after a session handshake
execution_modes.threads: the provider runs each role on one thread (local-threads: two threads in one process); Swanky spawns none of its own for this protocol

compile.note: cold = empty target dir, dependencies already fetched (--offline); warm_noop = the same command again; warm_leaf_rebuild = the provider example's source rewritten with identical bytes (new mtime), so only that example recompiles and relinks (with Swanky's -flto link args)

prep.fetch_note: fetch-cold starts from an empty CARGO_HOME (every crate and git dependency downloaded over the network); fetch-warm repeats it
prep.toolchain: Rust 1.99.0 (Swanky's rust-toolchain file) was installed before this run; install not measured

pq_classification.claim_ceiling: computation evidence under semi-honest, classical assumptions; no quantum soundness, side-channel, transport or settlement claim
classical_dependencies: base OT: Chou-Orlandi over Ristretto/curve25519 (discrete log): broken by a quantum adversary; its OT-extension security reduces to it, so this configuration is NOT post-quantum
pq_classification.configuration: popsicle circuit PSI as above, at swanky 409d1ceb
pq_classification.plonky3_comparison: not started: a later comparison must align the relation, public inputs, security target and proof-artifact requirements, and measure proof bytes as well as proving and verification cost
pq_classification.schmivitz: edge/schmivitz is a separate PQ-oriented research candidate (VOLE-in-the-head); a successful PSI run qualifies nothing about it, and a schmivitz run would qualify nothing about this PSI. Not built or run by this lane.
pq_classification.symmetric_components: AES-based correlation-robust hashing, PRG and garbling: quantum attacks are generic (Grover-type); no claim is made here

protocol_configuration.base_ot: swanky_ot_chou_orlandi (the alsz default type parameter): Chou-Orlandi OT over Ristretto, curve25519-dalek 5.0.0
protocol_configuration.comparison_width: PRIMARY_KEY_SIZE = 8 bytes: equality is tested on 64-bit OPPRF outputs inside the circuit
protocol_configuration.element_encoding: popsicle::utils::compress_and_hash_inputs: an element of at most 16 bytes is zero-padded into a 128-bit block, a longer one is SHA-256 truncated to 128 bits; then an AES-based correlation-robust hash, low byte masked off. Byte strings that differ only by trailing zero bytes collide (row char-length-ambiguity); the bench fixes the width at 8 bytes
protocol_configuration.garbling: swanky-twopac::semihonest Garbler/Evaluator over fancy_garbling::WireMod2 (binary garbled circuits)
protocol_configuration.hashing: evaluator: cuckoo hashing with NHASHES = 3 (base_psi/mod.rs), retried with a fresh key until placement succeeds; garbler: simple hashing into the same bins
observations: PsiGarbler::new and PsiEvaluator::new seed both the two-party-computation party (Garbler/Evaluator::new(channel, RNG::from_seed(seed))) and the base-PSI rng (RNG::from_seed(seed)) with the same seed, so the two RNG streams are identical (garbler.rs / evaluator.rs at the pin). The security impact is not analyzed here: UNVERIFIED.
protocol_configuration.opprf: swanky-oprf-kmprt (KMPRT OPPRF) for the primary keys
protocol_configuration.output_recipient: the evaluator (outputs() returns Some for the evaluator, None for the garbler)
permitted_leakage: the cardinality |A ∩ B|, to the evaluator
|B| (approximately): the evaluator sends its cuckoo bin count in the clear (base_psi/receiver.rs hash_data: channel.write(&cuckoo.nbins))
|B| through traffic volume (row leakage-evaluator-set-size); |A| likewise (char-garbler-larger sweep)
protocol_configuration.psi: popsicle::circuit_psi: PSTY19 circuit PSI (eprint 2019/241). OpprfPsiGarbler = PsiGarbler<_, OpprfSender>; OpprfPsiEvaluator = PsiEvaluator<_, OpprfReceiver>
protocol_configuration.security_mode: semi-honest: PsiGarbler and PsiEvaluator implement swanky_adversary::SemiHonest; no malicious-security variant is used

receipt_serialization.note: measured on a first pass of this receipt without this field; the final file differs only by this object and the finish timestamp

remaining_obligations: Malicious-security PSI: a different protocol configuration and a separate proof obligation.
Post-quantum base OT: the default ALSZ base OT is Chou-Orlandi over Ristretto (classical); see pq_classification.
Execution on independently controlled hosts with an authenticated transport (the TCP channel here is plaintext and unauthenticated).
Size-hiding: both set sizes leak through traffic volume and the cleartext bin count; padding to a public bound is not implemented.
Statistical correctness: comparisons on 64-bit OPPRF outputs; the false-positive bound is from source inspection, not measured.
The shared-seed observation in PsiGarbler::new / PsiEvaluator::new (protocol_configuration.observations) is recorded, not analyzed.
Settlement and authorization: this lane produces computation evidence only; bSiGner and bPay keep their bounded authorization and settlement roles.

session_policy.interrupted_sessions: no resumption: popsicle keeps all protocol state (base OTs, OT-extension state, garbling keys, OPPRF tables) in process memory, and the provider never writes it anywhere. An aborted, timed-out or killed session ends with its processes; a new session starts new processes, a new session id and new base OTs. Preprocessing (Garbler/Evaluator construction: base OT and OT-extension setup) is input-independent but is redone per session, never carried across sessions
session_policy.randomness: each role seeds its protocol RNG from OS entropy (SwankyRng::new); nothing is seeded by the harness, printed or persisted
session_policy.session_id: 128 bits from the OS random source per session, generated by rbench, bound by both roles in the handshake before any protocol byte; never reused (row session-ids-fresh)
